title: 精神疾患とその治療
subtitle: Psychiatric Disorders and Treatments
educationalGoal: Students will systematically understand the etiology, symptoms, diagnosis (DSM/ICD), course, and treatment methods (including the effects of pharmacotherapy and psychosocial support) of representative mental disorders. They will acquire knowledge of legal systems and social resources related to mental health and welfare, and understand multidisciplinary collaboration in medical settings as well as the role of certified psychologists within team-based care.
advice: This course aims to systematically learn the foundational knowledge regarding “mental disorders and their treatment” required of licensed psychologists. Based on the basic framework of psychiatry and mental health care, it provides an overview of representative mental disorders, covering conceptual understanding, clinical presentation (symptoms and course), approaches and procedures for diagnosis, and the objectives and methods of treatment. Treatment addresses both pharmacotherapy and psychosocial support, and students learn about the physical and psychological changes caused by psychotropic medications, as well as psychotherapy, rehabilitation, environmental adjustments, and the overall support systems that sustain community living. The course is conducted primarily through lectures, using textbooks, handouts, slides, and clinical case examples to deepen understanding (formats such as face-to-face or on-demand vary by university). Students are expected to read the assigned material in advance for each session, organize key points and questions, and attend class prepared. After class, it is important to review by organizing notes and materials and to relate terminology, concepts, and understanding of disorders (classification, diagnosis, treatment, and support). Since quizzes, reports, and worksheet submissions may be assigned, students are encouraged to articulate their understanding based on the lecture content and to actively ask questions both inside and outside of class. In particular, students aiming to become licensed psychologists should study with an awareness of collaboration with medical and related institutions, the role of psychologists in multidisciplinary teamwork, perspectives for supporting individuals and their families, and should also pay attention to systems, social resources, and ethical considerations (such as the protection of human rights).

achievementLevels.ideal: Able to systematically explain the diagnostic criteria, symptoms, and course of major disorders, and understands the names and side effects of psychotropic medications. Understands typical situations in which recommending a medical consultation (referral) is necessary, and has an overview of related laws and regulations such as the Mental Health and Welfare Act, as well as social resources. Is aware of the role of psychologists within multidisciplinary collaboration.
achievementLevels.standard: Able to systematically explain the diagnostic criteria, symptoms, and course of major disorders, and understands the names and side effects of psychotropic medications. Able to recognize the role of psychological professionals in multidisciplinary collaboration.

Based on the basic framework of psychiatry and mental health care, it provides an overview of representative mental disorders, covering conceptual understanding, clinical presentation (symptoms and course), approaches and procedures for diagnosis, and the objectives and methods of treatment. Treatment addresses both pharmacotherapy and psychosocial support, and students learn about the physical and psychological changes caused by psychotropic medications, as well as psychotherapy, rehabilitation, environmental adjustments, and the overall support systems that sustain community living. The course is conducted primarily through lectures, using textbooks, handouts, slides, and clinical case examples to deepen understanding (formats such as face-to-face or on-demand vary by university). Students are expected to read the assigned material in advance for each session, organize key points and questions, and attend class prepared. After class, it is important to review by organizing notes and materials and to relate terminology, concepts, and understanding of disorders (classification, diagnosis, treatment, and support). Since quizzes, reports, and worksheet submissions may be assigned, students are encouraged to articulate their understanding based on the lecture content and to actively ask questions both inside and outside of class. In particular, students aiming to become licensed psychologists should study with an awareness of collaboration with medical and related institutions, the role of psychologists in multidisciplinary teamwork, perspectives for supporting individuals and their families, and should also pay attention to systems, social resources, and ethical considerations (such as the protection of human rights).
